newsitem.title: USA: U.S. oil shares rise, led by Texaco results.
newsitem.headline: U.S. oil shares rise, led by Texaco results.

text.p: Shares of major U.S. oil companies rose after some third quarter results topped expectations despite weak refining and marketing.
Analysts said the rally was fueled by Texaco Inc which posted earnings of $1.61 per share, sharply above First Call estimates of $1.46.
"The market has been waiting for some positive surprises. There's definitely sector rotation in the market," said James Falvey of Smith Barney.

Shares of Texaco soared 2-3/4 to 106-1/8. Mobil Corp soared more than one in early trading but settled back by early afternoon, gaining 1/2 to 121-3/8. Exxon gained 3/8 to 89-3/4 and Amoco rose 5/8 to 75-1/2.

Analysts attributed Texaco's positive results to its heavy reliance on crude oil prices, which rose sharply in the third quarter. Also, Texaco, which sold its chemical operations in 1994, is no longer vulnerable to that sector's volatility.
"Their cost-cutting is finally paying off," said Jack Aydin of McDonald & Co Securities Inc.
However, Texaco and the other oil companies were hurt in the third quarter by refining and marketing margins, which failed to keep pace with the steep rise in crude prices.
